24.title: 2. Variables and Bindings
24.content: Immutable Bindings (let) . Variables defined with let are immutable. They cannot be reassigned. let name = "Alice" let count = 42 . A reassignment to a let binding is deliberately invalid. The documentation test requires the exact E_ASSIGN_IMMUTABLE diagnostic and verifies that no unsigned shortcut is produced: . let name = "Alice" name = "Bob" . Mutable Bindings (var) . Variables defined with var can be reassigned with = or compound assignment operators (+=, -=, *=, /=): . var counter = 0 counter += 1 counter = 10 . Type Annotations . Types are inferred automatically, but optional explicit type annotations can be supplied: . let message: Text = "Welcome" var total: Number = 0 var photos: List<Image> = [] .

25.title: 3. Strings & Text
25.content: Plain Strings . Enclosed in double quotes. Braces {} in plain strings are literal and are NOT interpolated. let greeting = "Hello, world!" let jsonTemplate = "{\"key\": \"value\"}" // braces are literal . Interpolated Strings (f"...") . Prefix with f. Expressions inside {} are parsed and evaluated. Literal braces are escaped as ``: . let name = "David" let count = 5 let message = f"User {name} has {count} items. Literal brace: " . Raw Strings (r"...") . Prefix with r. Backslashes are treated as literal characters: . let regex = r"\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b" . Multiline Strings ("""...""") . Enclosed in triple quotes: . let sql = """SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE active = true""" .

26.title: 4. Types and Collections
26.content: Primitive Types . | Text | Number (both integers and floating-point values) | Bool (true, false) | . Content Types . Native Apple Shortcuts content items: . | Image | File | URL | Date | Contact | CalendarEvent | AnyContent (arbitrary native Shortcut content) | . Collection Types . | List: List<T>, literal [item1, item2, item3]. Indexed starting at 0 (items[0]). | Map: Map<Text, V>, literal {"key": value}. | Record: Anonymous structural records { name: Text, age: Number }. | Optional: T?, e.g., Text? or Number?. Represented by none when absent. | Union: Small type unions Text | Number. | .

27.title: 5. Functions & Actions
27.content: Calling Actions . Actions in Cherri v2 accept an optional primary argument without label, followed by named arguments: . // Primary argument + named arguments let photo = selectPhotos() resizeImage(photo, width: 800, height: 600) // Named arguments only alert(alert: "Operation completed!", title: "Success") // Unlabeled primary argument show("Hello from Cherri v2!") . User-Defined Functions . function calculateDiscount(price: Number, percentage: Number = 10) -> Number { let discount = price * (percentage / 100) return price - discount } let finalPrice = calculateDiscount(100, percentage: 15) .

28.title: 6. Control Flow
28.content: Conditionals (if / else) . let count = 5 if count > 10 { show("More than 10 items") } else if count > 0 { show("Some items") } else { show("No items") } . Value-Producing if . let count = 5 let statusText = if count > 0 { yield f"{count} items remaining" } else { yield "Out of stock" } . Counting Loops (repeat) . repeat 3 as i { show(f"Iteration: {i}") } . Iteration Loops (for ... in) . let names = ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"] // Item only for item in names { show(item) } // Index (0-based) and item for (index, item) in names { show(f"#{index}: {item}") } . List-valued loop results . A value-producing repeat or for loop cannot currently preserve a separate nested List for each iteration. The native runtime probe produced four items from two two-item results. When the compiler knows that a loop would yield a List, it rejects that result with E_TARGET_VALUE_SHAPE and emits no shortcut: . let values = for item in [1, 2] { yield [item, "tail"] } . This boundary applies to the shape of the loop’s result. Statement loops and scalar results remain available. For results typed as AnyContent, successful compilation does not establish that nested List cardinality is preserved; that runtime case remains unverified. Menus (menu) . menu("Select an action") { case "Option 1" { show("Selected 1") } case "Option 2" { show("Selected 2") } } .

29.title: 7. Metadata and Shortcut Headers
29.content: Declare shortcut properties using the shortcut declaration: . shortcut "Network Routine" { icon: { glyph: 59789, color: 4282601983 } trigger wifi(event: .joined) } . Setup Questions . setup apiKey: Text { prompt: "Enter your API Key" default: "synthetic-key" } text(apiKey) . Setup questions are bound to one direct action parameter, as in text(apiKey). Declare a separate question for another slot. A declaration that is never used does not create a native import question. An authored Ask value is a runtime prompt; it is separate from a setup question.

30.title: 8. Native Escape Hatches
30.content: When exact plist keys or undocumented actions are required, use native: . let result = native.action( identifier: "com.apple.custom.action", parameters: { "CustomKey": "CustomValue", "Threshold": 100 } ) .

31.title: 9. CLI Tools
31.content: Check Code . Analyzes syntax and types without compiling: . cherri check my_shortcut.cherri cherri check my_shortcut.cherri --json . Format Code . Formats code using canonical Cherri style: . cherri format my_shortcut.cherri cherri format my_shortcut.cherri --write . Compiler Capabilities & Schema Metadata . Inspect supported features and action catalog fingerprint: . cherri --capabilities-json . Language Server (LSP) . Starts a standard JSON-RPC Language Server on stdin/stdout: . cherri lsp .

32.title: 10. Migration from Legacy Cherri
32.content: Use the official cherri-migrate tool to update legacy files: . cherri-migrate legacy.cherri --write . The migration tool: . | Converts @variable = ... to let or var based on reassignment analysis | Strips legacy #include statements | Converts string interpolation "Count {count}" to f"Count {count}" | Formats code canonically. | .

34.title: Cherri Language v2.0 Guide
34.content: Welcome to the Cherri Language v2.0 active authoring guide. The default public authoring path is V2. Existing Legacy programs remain available through the explicit –lang=legacy route; this section documents V2. Cherri v2.0 is an expressive, safe, strongly-typed language for authoring native Apple Shortcuts. It replaces legacy ad-hoc syntax with formal lexical and grammar rules, first-class interpolation, block-scoped variables, static typing, and direct native plist preservation.

35.title: Highlights of Language v2.0
35.content: . | Clean Modern Syntax: Declarative let (immutable) and var (mutable) bindings instead of @variables. | First-Class Interpolation: Clean f"Hello, {name}!" string interpolation preserving Apple’s WFTextTokenAttachment natively. | Strong Static Typing: Type checking with clear, actionable diagnostics (E_TYPE_MISMATCH, E_UNDEFINED_SYMBOL, E_ARG_UNKNOWN, etc.). | Deterministic Action Binding: Positional, named, and primary parameters resolved deterministically against the Action Registry. | Rich Control Flow: if / else if / else, repeat(n), for item in list, and menu statements. | Safety First: Deprecated legacy constructs (#include, @var, const) produce explicit migration errors pointing to modern replacements. | .

45.title: 1. Automated Migration with cherri-migrate
45.content: Cherri v2 includes an AST-aware migration CLI tool: cherri-migrate. Usage . # Preview migrated output to stdout cherri-migrate my_shortcut.cherri # Apply migration changes directly to the file cherri-migrate my_shortcut.cherri --write . The migration tool automatically: . | Replaces @var declarations with let or var based on reassignment analysis. | Removes legacy #include directives. | Upgrades interpolation strings "Hello {name}" to f"Hello {name}". | Canonicalizes formatting. | .

46.title: 2. Before and After Examples
46.content: Variable Declarations . Cherri v1 (Legacy reference): . @name = "Alice" const greeting = "Hello" @count = 0 @count = @count + 1 . Cherri v2.0 (Modern): . let name = "Alice" let greeting = "Hello" var count = 0 count = count + 1 . String Interpolation . Cherri v1 (Legacy reference): . @city = "Tel Aviv" show("Welcome to {city}!") . Cherri v2.0 (Modern): . let city = "Tel Aviv" show(f"Welcome to {city}!") . Plain strings "Welcome to {city}!" now preserve literal braces. To interpolate, prepend f to the string literal. Action Calls & Named Arguments . Cherri v1 (Legacy reference): . resizeImage(@photo, 800, 600) . Cherri v2.0 (Modern): . let photo = selectPhotos() resizeImage(photo, width: 800, height: 600) . In Cherri v2, the primary argument is passed positionally and subsequent arguments use parameter labels for clarity and deterministic binding. Indexing . Cherri v1 (Legacy reference): . @first = @list[1] // 1-based indexing . Cherri v2.0 (Modern): . let values = ["first", "second"] let first = values[0] // 0-based indexing . Collections and lists now consistently use standard 0-based indexing.

47.title: 3. Legacy Syntax Diagnostic Codes
47.content: If you attempt to compile Cherri v1 code with cherri v2.0, the compiler will emit explicit diagnostic errors: . | Legacy Syntax | Diagnostic Code | Remediation | . | @var | E_LEGACY_SYNTAX | Replace with let var = ... or var var = ... | . | const var | E_LEGACY_SYNTAX | Replace with let var = ... | . | #include "..." | E_LEGACY_SYNTAX | Remove #include | . Run cherri check <file> to view all diagnostics with file locations and remediation hints.
